5.2.2 Fauna and Water Quality
Construction of the proposed pumped storage project would eliminate wildlife habitat from approximately 505 acres of land, including 370 acres that would be inundated by the reservoir. Approximately 95 acres of wildlife habitat would be lost due to construction of access roads, tunnel portals, and a transmission line tie station. The proposed construction yard would temporarily remove approximately 40 acres of land from its existing use as habitat until vegetative cover became reestablished. Approximately 315 acres of additional land would be affected to establish the transmission line rights-of-way.
Wildlife populations in the areas of inundation, construction, and clearing would experience several unavoidable adverse environmental effects. These effects would vary, depending on the wildlife species present and the type and the quality of any mitigative or enhancement measures taken. Deer, bear, turkey, and other wildlife species using any of the areas to be altered would lose a portion or all of their habitat. Wildlife populations in areas suffering complete habitat destruction would be forced to move to other areas providing suitable habitat. Some losses would result, especially to the less mobile forms of wildlife, those that do not leave the project area, and those that move to adjacent areas which are presently at their maximum carrying capacity.
Quantitative estimates of the numbers of wildlife adversely affected are not available. Estimates of existing wildlife populations in and adjacent to the proposed project area would be necessary to estimate the populations affected by the proposed action. The ability of adjacent wildlife habitat to support displaced wildlife would need to be determined in order to predict quantitative effects of the project on wildlife. Should the adjacent areas be unable to support the displaced wildlife, these individuals would be lost.
